text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- An aircraft with 47 Bosnian refugees expelled from Germany, arrives at Sarajevo airport. They said they were informed of their expulsion only two days beforehand.

- Bosnian minister for refugees accuses international High Representative to Bosnia Carl Bildt of obstructing return of Croat and Moslem refugees to disputed town of Brcko together with Bosnian Serb authorities.
- Chairman of Bosnia's collective presidency Alija Izetbegovic received 1996 International Democracy Award by the Centre for Democracy in New York.
- British agency for Overseas development (ODA) has spent 170 million pounds for humanitarian projects in Bosnia, Baroness Linda Chalker says.
- Claude Ganz, U.S. president's special envoy to Bosnia, believes that if the international community continues to provide only aid to Bosnia its economic reconstruction won't ever be realised.
- Ganz says that taxes in Bosnia are extremely high and threaten to bury economy.
- Moslem co-chairman of Bosnia's joint cabinet Haris Silajdzic holds talks with Egyptian president Hosni Mubarak on bilateral co- operation and support from Islamic world to Bosnia.

- One man was killed in shooting incident in Sarajevo restaurant. Police say victim earlier threatened to shoot opposition politician Nijaz Durakovic and his associates. Durakovic's bodyguard shot the 20-year old man, who died on the way to hospital. Another man was seriously wounded. Police arrested the bodyguard. -- Sarajevo newsroom, +387-71-663-864
